(2) The capture-stale PAGE is observed EXECUTING — a `Telegram alert` step reaching a non-skipped conclusion — whether from a genuinely stale capture or from a deliberate exercise that makes capture_bad true. ⚠️ A GREEN RUN WITH BOTH ALERT STEPS `skipped` IS THE HEALTHY CASE AND CLEARS (2) NOT AT ALL; that is what every run so far has been, so 'it passed again' is not progress on this half. ⚠️ AND THE STEP REPORTING `success` IS NOT THE OPERATOR RECEIVING IT — that distinction keeps other rows in this file open; record which of the two you established. ⚠️ IF THE OPERATOR DECIDES the 6-hourly cadence is wrong, or that the watcher should not run, this row does NOT clear — it CHANGES: the capture is then unwatched on a schedule, which is a legitimate decision and must be RECORDED as one rather than left looking like a cadence about to start.
items.why_it_cannot_be_closed_by_time: The capture is FORWARD-ONLY: an hour it does not write is an hour nothing can re-derive, so the cost of a cadence that never starts accrues silently and is unrecoverable. Waiting does not produce the scheduled run — only reading the run history establishes whether one happened.

FOUR DECISIONS TAKEN 2026-08-29, recorded here so no session re-asks them. The operator's complaint that prompted this — that cash had been said 'a million times' — is the cost of NOT having recorded it. (1) FUNDING MODE: CASH. Consequences that follow and are NOT re-litigable: no shorting, gross-exposure multiple can never exceed 1.0x so max_gross_exposure_pct is decorative, and PDT is INERT (BL-20260823-NO-PDT-MODELLING-ON-ALPACA does not apply under this branch). (2) SIZE BOUND: a per-trade cap expressed as a PERCENT OF EQUITY, not a fixed dollar figure — chosen so it scales if the account is later funded rather than going stale, and so oversized intents are sized DOWN and still place rather than being refused by the venue. Value not yet chosen; Tier-3. (3) T+1: MODEL IT BEFORE ANY LEG GOES LIVE. The operator declined the cheaper 'restrict to 1d legs and defer' option I recommended. This is the blocker this row tracks. (4) FUNDING AMOUNT: keep $200.10 for now; revisit after real fills reconcile. At the 0.9 cash wall that is ~$180 usable, so any instrument priced above it is mechanically untradeable at one whole share — indicative prices from the retracted Phase 3 doc put GLD ~$423 and SPY ~$640 in that category, NOT re-measured. ROSTER INTENT: one cheap, affordable, non-USO, daily-cadence leg as an explicit PLUMBING TEST — to prove fills reconcile against exchange truth, that whole-share sizing behaves on a cash book, and that silent_refusal_alert grades the account healthy. It is NOT an edge bet and must not be reported as one: stripped of uso_trend_1h (excluded from real money on standing non-financial grounds), the 16-leg candidate set has NO positive measured record on either paper population. The specific leg is not yet chosen and adding it is Tier-3 in its own right — alpaca_live is mode: live with strategies: [], so that empty list is the ENTIRE gate and the first leg added IS the live-trading moment, with no mode flip in front of it. 

UPDATE 2026-08-29 (same day, later): THE MODEL SHIPPED — PR #10408, `src/runtime/cash_settlement.py`, merged and deployed (VM confirmed on the merge sha, restart_pending false). Basis is `min(venue_buying_power, venue_cash - our_unsettled)`, which is correct under all four combinations of (Alpaca nets unsettled proceeds / does not) x (we saw the sale / did not) — asserted as a 4-case parametrized test, because the distinguishing state has NEVER existed on this account (cash == buying_power == regt_buying_power == equity == 200.10, all four identical) and both paper mirrors are MARGIN accounts that cannot exhibit cash-account behaviour. Trading days come from the venue's own /v2/calendar because src/runtime/market_hours.py models no holidays and counting T+1 with it would credit proceeds a day EARLY across a holiday, manufacturing the violation. 

THE REMAINING TWO DECISIONS ARE ALSO NOW TAKEN (2026-08-29, popups): per-trade cap = 100%, i.e. NO cap beyond the cash account's own 1.0x limit; `risk_pct` STAYS 0.05. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-31: that half is STALE and was stale in the dangerous direction — do NOT re-quote it. Decision (2) in the block above is therefore RESOLVED and its 'value not yet chosen' is stale. Why that pair is coherent rather than reckless at this size, so nobody 'fixes' it: the sizer demands ~26.7 TLT shares (~11x the account) and the CASH BALANCE clamps it to 2, so realised risk at the declared stop is ~$0.75, not the $10 the 5% implies — confirmed by the observed qty 2.0 journal rows, not inferred. WHY THIS ROW STILL DOES NOT CLEAR, and what would: `clears_when` asks for a would-be order REFUSED with a logged cause. At `annotate` the gate computes and writes a soak row and changes no sizing, so it can never produce that observation. WARNING FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: `would_have_reduced_usd` will read 0.00 on alpaca_live however long anyone waits — `recent_sales` requires status='closed' with a non-null exit price inside a 10-day window and that account has NONE (all 23 recent rows are `rejected`; its last real position closed in July). The mechanism evidence lives on the PAPER accounts, which do sell — 6 closed sales in 10 days, up to $111,069.37. 

A REPO TIMER NOW CARRIES THE PRECONDITION: PR #10412 adds `.github/workflows/alpaca-settlement-soak-watch.yml`, weekdays 14:30 UTC. It grades the soak against the newest alpaca dispatch FIRST, so an empty soak is never collapsed: `not_yet_exercised` (no dispatch since deploy — silent, not a failure) vs `never_wrote` (a dispatch DID happen — a finding, fails the job). This cannot separate those: with GPU_BURST_ARMED != 1 the workflow runs a DRY PREFLIGHT ONLY, and its log carries the same step name as an armed run. So a pass means 'a run exists that reached the preflight step', and a session must read that run's own output to see whether it was armed and what it decided. The literal is deliberately the step name rather than a decision string, because no decision string has ever been observed in a real run — inventing one would be a predicate matching nothing while looking precise. Tighten it to the real decision line the first time an armed run happens. Since the event never occurs spontaneously, a FAIL here means 'nobody has fired one', not 'the gate is broken'.

items.observation:
WHY THIS EXISTS. `render_session_brief` calls `datetime.now()` and `due_items` flips a monitoring row to DUE once `check_every_days` elapses, so the block COMMITTED in CLAUDE.md goes stale at a UTC-midnight boundary with no commit anywhere. The whole-tree `--check` then reds EVERY open PR until a human re-renders, and nothing re-runs a branch's checks, so a branch cut inside that window is stranded permanently.

MEASURED 2026-08-31, not inferred: OI-20260826-MHG-OVER-COVER-MECHANISM-UNVERIFIED (verified_at 2026-08-29, check_every_days 2) crossed into DUE at 00:00Z. PRs #10538 (00:47Z) and #10539 (01:22Z) BOTH failed on exactly `session-brief-guard` — read from the job logs, not guessed — with pytest-run, pytest-collect and repo-inventory GREEN on both. CLAUDE.md was not re-rendered until 06:47Z. Merging current main into each branch (operator-approved) turned `guards` GREEN on both with no content change, which is the positive control that the cause was the clock and not their rows.

STATE THE POPULATION: 2 of the 3 stranded automation PRs were inspected. #10398 was NOT examined (operator said do not touch it), so it is NOT claimed to share this cause.

WHAT IS NOT YET PROVEN: every test of the fix is synthetic — a temp git repo built by tests/test_session_brief_diff_scope.py. No REAL CI run has printed `verdict=inherited`, which is the only evidence the diff-scoped path behaves on a live PR (a `--base origin/main` that cannot resolve in the guards job would grade `base_unreadable` and FAIL CLOSED — the same red as before, for a different reason, which is exactly the confusion this row exists to catch). The one-shot `commit-to-main` refresh is likewise unexercised: no run has reported a `stale-branch refresh -> ...` notice.

=== 2026-08-31, HALF (a) STILL OPEN; THE FINDING CLAUSE IS RULED OUT. ===
The diff-scoped guard ran in real CI twice on PR #10575 (`guards` green on both 00cfb57e and
d4f4c745, with `--check --base origin/main`). It printed `clean`, NOT `inherited` — the brief
was current on both sides, so half (a) is genuinely unmet rather than quietly satisfied.
⚠️ But the FINDING this row names — `verdict=base_unreadable`, i.e. origin/main not resolving
in the guards job — DID NOT OCCUR. That was the specific risk of shipping a ref-dependent
check, and it is now ruled out by observation rather than by reasoning.
Half (b) also unmet, correctly: the dispatcher's stamp PR (#10576) merged without stalling,
so the one-shot refresh had nothing to do and printed no `stale-branch refresh ->` line.
Neither half can be forced; both need a PR that opens across a cadence boundary.
items.clears_when: BOTH: (a) a real CI run prints `session-brief: verdict=inherited` on a PR that did not touch the registers, found in that run's job log rather than reasoned about; and (b) a `commit-to-main` run prints `stale-branch refresh -> refreshed` or `-> not_needed_up_to_date`, proving the branch is on the new code path at all. A passing synthetic test is NEITHER half. If instead a run prints `verdict=base_unreadable`, that is a FINDING — `origin/main` is not resolvable in the guards job — and the fix is the ref, not this row.

probe.checks: BOTH halves, in the two DIFFERENT workflows that print them, because clears_when requires both and a pass on one half is the over-read this family exists to prevent. (a) `session-brief: verdict=inherited` in a guards.yml run — emitted only by render_session_brief.py's inherited branch, so its presence IS the diff-scoping path having been taken on a real PR. (b) `commit-to-main: stale-branch refresh ->` in a due-list.yml run — the composite action prints it with the resulting state, proving the automation branch is on the new code path at all. Each group is scanned over the last 20 runs and EVERY group must hit. The positive control `session-brief:` appears in essentially every guards run, so a workflow rename, an expired log or a revoked token becomes could_not_look instead of a permanent quiet negative.
probe.is_not: A pass does NOT establish that half (a) came from a PR that genuinely did not touch the registers — the log line does not carry the diff, and `inherited` is explicitly NOT 'the brief is fine', it is 'this PR did not break it'. Nor does it tell which of `-> refreshed` and `-> not_needed_up_to_date` half (b) printed; clears_when accepts either, but they mean different things and a session grading the mechanism should read which. ⚠️ THIS READER HAS NEVER RUN AGAINST THE REAL ACTIONS API: api.github.com is intercepted at HTTP 403 from a Claude Code on the web sandbox, so its controls run against a fake server and its FIRST scheduled run is its real verification. That is safe only because a broken reader here reports could_not_run, never fail — if this row shows could_not_run after the probes workflow has run, suspect the reader before the mechanism. Finally, clears_when's own escape hatch stands: a run printing `verdict=base_unreadable` is a FINDING about the ref, not evidence for this row, and no probe makes that call.

items.summary: scope-overlap-audit works — its FIRST GENUINE catch landed 2026-08-31T17:26Z. But the same comment ALSO reported this session's own board START back at it, because the attributor compares the START's branch to the PR's branch and a session posts ONE START while opening PRs from SEVERAL branches. Read an overlap comment expecting one line of it to be yours.
items.clears_when: A scope-overlap comment on a PR from a session that posted its START under a DIFFERENT branch name lists that START under the `mine` attribution (i.e. it is NOT rendered as another session's) — read from the comment body. The proposed fix is a session-suffix match; any fix that achieves the above clears this.
items.observation: MEASURED 2026-08-31T17:26:46Z on PR #10607, read from the posted comment, not from the code. It reported `Compared 3 changed file(s) against 66 declared path(s) — 6 attributed to another session, 2 unattributable`. THE GENUINE HALF IS REAL AND IS THE FIRST ONE: `claude/research-queue-landing-v4yfq7` (11:41Z, 15:24Z) and `claude/research-disposition-resweep-cplgnv` (15:55Z) had both declared `docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json`, and the latter also `ROADMAP.md` and `docs/sprint-logs/` — all three files this PR changes. That supersedes any claim that the detector has never caught a real overlap; it has. THE DEFECT IS THE THIRD LINE: `claude/workflows-audit-restructure-fz0sw9` is THIS session's own designated branch, and the PR was opened from `claude/session-wrapup-fz0sw9`, so `attribution()`'s `branch == my_branch` test graded the session's own START as `other`. This is the SAME false-positive class fixed in #10594, in a narrower form — that fix handled a START with no branch; this is a START with a DIFFERENT branch from the same session. It is the COMMON shape, not an edge case: a session posts one START and opens per-task branches. PROPOSED FIX (small, not applied here): the trailing 6-char session suffix is shared across a session's branches (`fz0sw9`, `v4yfq7`, `cplgnv`), so match on that suffix in addition to the exact branch. It must ADD to `mine`, never suppress an `other` — under-reporting a real overlap is the worse error, which is why the `unattributable` state already resolves toward reporting. ⚠️ NOT A BLOCKER FOR #10607: the overlap was verified harmless — those sessions' work had already merged (#10602, #10604) and `git merge-tree` against `origin/main` was CLEAN.

Measured all three arms (no-pipefail rc=0 / pipefail SKIPPED rc=141 / control TAKEN). Fixed by capturing --help once and matching with `case`. ⚠️ THIS IS THE THREE-STATE CONTRACT WORKING, NOT FAILING: #10597 exists so `benchmarked` is never printed over a generation step that did not run, and it was not — the run graded itself and named which half is valid. OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-31: RE-RUN for the answer. It is queued against main once the SIGPIPE fix lands (PR #10620) and costs a full llama.cpp rebuild plus a 2 GB re-download on the 1-core trainer under the heavy lock — the EXIT trap cleaned up, disk back to 7.4 G. || 2026-09-01 (session 01HYXKHpDQeWv3u4rjWWoL2J): THE RE-RUN COMPLETED AND THE ANSWER IS NOW MEASURED — the row is READY FOR THE OPERATOR'S DECISION and is NOT cleared by me, because clears_when ends 'Then the operator decides.' Collected via trainer-diag #10642 off the run launched 2026-08-31T22:11:17Z, finished 22:27:49Z. BOTH CONTROLS PASS, which is what makes the sample gradeable at all: `single-shot flag: -st` (the SIGPIPE fix in #10620 works — the previous run's `benchmarked_throughput_only` is gone) and `RESULT: benchmarked`. DONE marker present, no process running, lock released, EXIT trap cleaned up (disk 7.4G). Throughput on the real generation path: pp128 9.67 +/- 1.27, tg64 3.91 +/- 0.00 t/s; end-to-end 10.5 t/s prompt / 3.7 t/s generation; 200 tokens in 71.07s wall at 96% CPU; peak RSS 4,947,364 KB = 4.95 GB on the 5.9 GB box, ~0.96 GB headroom. Consistent with the earlier throughput-only arm (10.57 / 3.91), so the speed answer has not moved: ~2.1x and ~1.84x slower than the 1.5B.

THE ANSWER, WHICH IS THE DELIVERABLE. Same prompt as the 1.5B baseline. THE 3B IS BETTER ON BOTH SPECIFIC DEFECTS THE 1.5B WAS FAILED FOR, and that is a real improvement rather than a hedge: (1) NO FABRICATED CAUSAL CLAIM — where the 1.5B joined two unrelated facts with an invented 'indicating', the 3B hedges correctly ('This suggests a discrepancy', 'could indicate issues with the margin calculation process'); (2) NO MISATTRIBUTION — the 1.5B blamed venue liquidity, while the 3B keeps the fault on the internal side ('the margin calculation process', 'the margin management system'), which is where the defect actually was. ⚠️ BUT IT NEVER NAMES THE MECHANISM. The real cause is that the sizer fell back to TOTAL EQUITY and counted initial margin already pledged to open positions as free (BL-20260813-ICTSCALP-BTC-BYBIT2-BALANCE-REJECTS, fixed by the coin_derived rung). The 3B produces generic-competent prose that restates the prompt and gestures at 'a discrepancy' — nothing a session could act on. ⚠️ AND CORRECT ONE THING IN THE BASELINE ABOVE: it attributes the 1.5B's truncation to the model ('TRUNCATED mid-sentence without answering the third of the prompt asking what to check next'). THE 3B TRUNCATES AT THE SAME PLACE — 3 complete bullets then a severed '- **Next Steps to' — and the cause is OURS, not the model's: the harness passes `-n 200`, a generation cap both runs hit. Truncation is therefore NOT evidence about either model and must not be counted against the 3B or re-quoted against the 1.5B; raising `-n` is the fix if the 'what to check next' third is ever to be graded.

SO THE MEASURED VERDICT IS: better where it was failed, still not useful, at ~2x the cost and ~1 GB of headroom on a 1-core box. My reading is that this does not carry weight for analysis work on a system whose canonical rule is always-verify — plausible generic prose is the failure mode that rule exists to catch — but the decision is the operator's and the row stays open for it.

items.summary: The TELEGRAM half of the decision round-trip is built (src/runtime/telegram_decisions.py + a `wdec:*` branch in telegram_query_bot.callback_handler + a job-queue sweep): an unanswered `decision_requests[]` entry is sent to the operator as an inline-keyboard prompt, and a tap POSTs to /api/bot/work/decision over loopback. items.detail: What a harness HAS established (tests/test_telegram_decisions.py, 73 passing): callback_data is 26 bytes fixed against Telegram's 64-byte cap for ids up to 2000 chars; the option token is a digest of the option KEY so reordering the options does not silently select a different answer (a positional index would have); a digest collision is refused rather than resolved by first match; the success reply says `Submitted - NOT yet decided` and the string `committed` does not appear in it; every refusal path states that nothing was submitted, and the one genuinely ambiguous case (no HTTP response at all) says it does NOT know rather than claiming either way; the sweep asks once, only for `not_submitted`, and HOLDS rather than sending buttons that would 503. What a harness CANNOT reach is every stage that matters here: no message has been rendered in Telegram, no button has been tapped, and no submission has travelled the loopback POST. TWO ENVIRONMENT FACTS ARE INFERRED AND NOT MEASURED. (1) DASHBOARD_API_TOKEN is written by scripts/ops/sync_vm_secrets.sh into /home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/.env, which is exactly the EnvironmentFile deploy/ict-telegram-bot.service reads -- so the bot SHOULD hold the bearer, but this session could not read that process's environment (no issue_write, so no `get-env` system-action) and did not verify it. If it is absent the sweep HOLDS and logs a WARNING rather than sending dead buttons; it does not fail open. (2) The destination is the trader bot (TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN), chosen because ict-telegram-bot.service is the process that POLLS it. probe.checks: A bybit_coverage_soak row exists in which the SIDE-AWARE grade actually DISAGREED with the side-blind sum (verdicts_differ: true). That is the load-bearing half of this row's threshold: a soak of any length in which the two never diverge shows the gate would change nothing on this book, so a bare row COUNT is not the criterion and the probe deliberately does not test one. The positive control (verdicts_differ present as either true or false) is what separates 'the gate ran and always agreed' from 'the log is absent or unreadable' -- and here that distinction is load-bearing rather than decorative, because 'nothing matched' is the state this row is ALREADY expected to be in, so an unreadable log would emit exactly the answer a reader anticipates. Measured 2026-09-02 the whole file held 28 rows, all with verdicts_differ false, so the control passes today while the requirement does not.
probe.is_not: A PASS DOES NOT CLEAR THIS ROW, and specifically does not satisfy either clause of clears_when. It cannot see the ROW COUNT or the DAY SPAN (>=20 rows over >=3 distinct UTC days), because probe_soak tests for the existence of a matching row and not for a distribution -- so a single disagreement on one day passes this probe and clears nothing. It also cannot make clause (b), which is an OPERATOR DECISION to arm or not to arm; no probe can stand in for that. [!] A FAIL IS NOT EVIDENCE THE GATE IS INERT EITHER: the honest reading of a fail is 'no disagreement has been observed YET', and distinguishing that from 'this gate would never disagree' needs the day span the probe cannot measure. [!] AND IT SAYS NOTHING ABOUT WHETHER THE GATE IS ARMED -- it reads the annotate-mode soak, which is written whether or not BYBIT_GRADED_COVERAGE_ACCOUNTS names an account. Arming is confirmed on /proc/<MainPID>/environ via get-env, never from this log and never from the .env file.

items.clears_when: THE SOAK THRESHOLD IS STATED SO THIS CANNOT BE CLEARED BY IMPATIENCE OR RUN FOREVER. Clears when BOTH: (a) the soak log holds at least 20 graded rows spanning at least 3 distinct UTC days on at least one Bybit account, AND at least one row where the side-aware grade DIFFERS from the side-blind sum (verdicts_differ true); and (b) the operator, shown that row count and at least one concrete disagreement, decides to arm or not to arm. [!] A COUNT OF ROWS IS NOT THE CRITERION ON ITS OWN: 20 rows in which every grade agrees means the gate is inert on this book, and arming it would be a change with no measured effect. Record that and say so rather than arming to close the row. [!] DECIDING NOT TO ARM CLEARS THIS ROW TOO, and must be RECORDED as a decision rather than left looking like a soak still running: that is the failure mode the rule exists to catch. [!] AN EMPTY SOAK DOES NOT CLEAR IT AND IS ITSELF THE FINDING: zero rows after 3 days means the code is not deployed or not reached, which is a deploy defect, not a quiet book. Zero rows and twenty-agreeing rows are opposite facts and must never both be reported as 'the soak is quiet'.

items.detail: WHY THE BRIEF IS REGENERATED IN THE SAME RUN, because it looks like housekeeping and is not: render_session_brief.py READS docs/claude/CONSTRAINT.json. A cron that advanced the readout alone would leave CLAUDE.md quoting the PREVIOUS headline under a NEW file's date -- i.e. it would RELOCATE this staleness into the one surface that reaches a session before it acts, which is strictly worse than the bug it replaces. The two are committed together, always. !! A STALENESS GUARD WAS DELIBERATELY NOT USED INSTEAD. A `--check` on freshness would red every open PR whenever the world moved, which is BL-20260830-A-TRANSIENT-RED-BASE-PERMANENTLY-STRANDS-AN-AUTOMERGE-BRANCH and is why session-brief-guard had to be diff-scoped against origin/main. Do not 'strengthen' this by adding one. !! A FAILED RUN IS WATCHED: the workflow is in claude-run-failure-alert.yml's list, enforced by scripts/ci/check_cron_failure_watch.py, so a dead run pages rather than going silent -- but that watches FAILURE, not ABSENCE, and a cron that never fires produces neither.

items.detail: WHY THIS COULD NOT BE SEEN BEFORE, and why the repair was worth doing even though it does not fix the cause. THE PROXY IS A PROXY AND IS LABELLED AS ONE. Branch quiescence indicates HAND-BACK; it is not proof of one, because a session can be alive with nothing pushed. So the watcher never claims a session is dead and never merges, closes, un-drafts or comments — the same reason session_reaper.py is permitted to grade the same proxy ('the cost of calling a live session stalled_with_work is a refreshed row in a ledger').
